newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast sets diamond deal with Carnegie.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast sets diamond deal with Carnegie.

text.p: Ivory Coast has formed a diamond exploration syndicate with Australia's Carnegie Minerals NL with terms for potential joint production in the north of the country, a government statement said.

"Negotiations between Sodemi (state mining agency) and the Australian firm Carnegie Minerals have ended with a syndicate agreement for diamond mineral exploration as well as other useful mineral substances," said the statement, issued after a cabinet meeting late on Thursday.
Exploration would centre on Bobi in the Seguela diamond region where two other deposits are already being mined.
The venture gives Carnegie 65 percent of the shares, Sodemi 25 percent, and the government the rest.
"In the event of a definitive feasibility study, Sodemi and Carnegie agree to form a development company for working the deposit or deposits discovered," the statement said.
Under the agreement, Carnegie has agreed to invest at least 212.5 million CFA francs ($350,000) in the first three-year permit period.
Ivory Coast has been encouraging mining investment since 1995, when it issued a revised mining code, to broaden its largely cocoa and coffee dominated farm economy.
Local dealers put annual Ivorian diamond production at 25,000 carats of medium-to-low grade diamonds destined mainly for export to Antwerp and sale for industrial usage.
Official mining data for main resource deposits from gold to bauxite gave no figure for diamonds.
Other mining projects planned in Ivory Coast include a third gold mine in late 1997 and a large nickel project shortly after 2000.
About 65 mining exploration permits have been issued to over 25 companies, many of which have arrived since the revision of the mining code. ($ = 620 CFA francs)
